name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent David Taylor running with ~$1.1M raised
model.rationale: The R+21 district, a well-funded incumbent, and a Democratic challenger with essentially no campaign resources all point to a safe Republican hold; prediction markets agree at roughly 98% Republican. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with no evidence favoring an upset.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending against Taylor would be the first sign of a competitive race, though none is currently present.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 2nd District is a heavily Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent David Taylor is running for reelection after clearing his primary, and he has raised roughly $1.1 million with about $443,000 on hand. His Democratic opponent, Jennifer Mazzuckelli, has reported only about $1,000 raised and $219 on hand, leaving her with no visible campaign infrastructure.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 98 percent. With the incumbent advantage, the funding gap, and the district's lean all pointing the same direction, this race is rated Safe Republican.
